case.pattern_description: Coordinated online micro-billing scheme targeting multiple unrelated cardholders across 20+ accounts in the same period. Transactions consist of repeated low-value authorizations under $10 for product C spaced over multiple weeks without an escalating high-value purchase. The identical authorization signature and sequential transaction numbering across customers indicate an automated card enumeration or illicit subscription skimming campaign.

evidence.claim: Customer reported: Customer C12975 message: 'I did not make these charges on my card. Please look into it.' Refers to 3660260.

Card C12975-K2 made 6 online product-C charges totalling $23.99 over 21.2 days (3660255, 3660256, 3660257, 3660258, 3660259, 3660260); in its 60 transactions of the 60 days before, that kind made up 0%. Every one is a tiny authorisation, spread over days with no larger purchase after them, so they are not R5's sequence of three within an hour followed by a purchase.

20 other cards (20 other customers) newly show the same signature in the 30 days to the alert - 3+ online authorisations under $10, on a card that had not made such charges before - against 8 and 4 in the same window one and two months earlier: C05083-K1, C00348-K1, C09471-K2, C01326-K2, C03611-K2, C04105-K2, C04528-K1, C05704-K2, C08972-K1, C09582-K1, C10035-K2, C11332-K1.

evidence.claim: Card C12975-K2 experienced an abrupt behavioural shift with an unprecedented run of 6 online micro-authorizations under $10 for product C between 2017-01-05 and 2017-01-26 totaling $23.99, departing from its established baseline of in-person product W transactions.
Card C12975-K2 was previously compromised in closed case CC-4890 in October 2016 for card-not-present fraud involving unrecognized online purchases totaling $800.03.

Transaction 3660259 in the micro-charge run was executed using device D000168, a generic desktop IE 11 profile associated with 45 cards in the window and 41 historical closed fraud cases including CC-5084.

The micro-authorizations on card C12975-K2 were spaced across 21 days rather than clustered within one hour, and were not followed by a large authorization over $100, which does not fit standard Rule R5 card testing.

Region 337 is familiar to card C12975-K2, accounting for 28 prior transactions (14.1% of card history), and shows no elevated fraud concentration with a lift of only 0.14 vs base rate in the 7-day window.

The alert text also contained 2 segment(s) addressed to the system rather than an analyst (outcome_directive, override, role_marker). They were set aside and used neither as evidence nor as instruction; the decision rests on the evidence above.

case.summary: Customer C12975 reported unauthorized activity after transaction 3660260 was flagged, uncovering an episode of six online micro-authorizations for product C totaling $23.99 between January 5 and January 26, 2017. These charges represent an unprecedented departure from the cardholder's established baseline of in-person product W transactions. Graph analysis revealed an identical micro-authorization signature across 20 other cards and customers active in the same 30-day period. Transaction 3660259 was conducted via device D000168, which is tied to 41 prior fraud cases, and card C12975-K2 was previously compromised in case CC-4890. The activity was confirmed as an undocumented coordinated micro-billing fraud scheme, resulting in card blockage, scheme monitoring, and regulatory reporting.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details a coordinated online micro-billing fraud scheme identified on account card C12975-K2, belonging to customer C12975. Between January 5, 2017, and January 26, 2017, six unauthorized online transactions totaling $23.99 for product C were processed against card C12975-K2. The individual transactions comprise 3660255 ($3.51), 3660256 ($5.18), 3660257 ($2.66), 3660258 ($4.75), 3660259 ($4.99), and 3660260 ($2.90). All six transactions occurred in the card-not-present online channel, originating from billing regions 191 and 337. On January 26, 2017, customer C12975 formally alerted the financial institution disavowing transaction 3660260 and confirming that they did not authorize the charges. Historical analysis revealed that card C12975-K2 had no prior history of online product C purchases, as its established baseline consisted exclusively of in-person retail product W transactions. One of the transactions, 3660259, was conducted using device D000168, a desktop Internet Explorer 11 profile that has appeared across 45 cards and 41 prior confirmed fraud cases, including case CC-5084. Furthermore, graph network analysis identified an identical pattern of low-value online micro-authorizations under $10 across 20 other customer cards, including peer cards C05083-K1, C00348-K1, and C09471-K2 during the same 30-day timeframe. The low monetary values, extended multi-week spacing, and parallel occurrence across unrelated accounts indicate an automated card enumeration or illicit subscription skimming campaign designed to evade velocity controls. In response to this confirmed compromise, card C12975-K2 was blocked to prevent further loss, the 20 connected peer accounts were flagged for monitoring, and internal case HHF-004 was escalated for comprehensive scheme tracking.

stop_reason: The investigation was stopped pursuant to Policy Section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.941, exceeding the decisive threshold, supported by multiple independent evidentiary bases including an acute cardholder behavioral shift, cross-card links to 20 peer accounts, and device linkage to historical fraud cases. Under policy guidelines, additional verification steps were unnecessary as they would not alter the final actions to block the card, monitor connected cards, and file a regulatory report.
